Scheme: The certificate number format "R49/2013-FR2-16.02" — scheme A vs B. R49/2013-FR2-16.02: This is an OIML-CS certificate. The "FR2" indicates France as issuing authority. Scheme... Typically the certificate number format for scheme A is "Rxx/yyyy-A-xx-xx" and scheme B... Actually in OIML-CS, certificate numbers look like "R60/2000-FR-03.12" for scheme A? Let me think. OIML-CS certificates: e.g. "R 60/2000-DE-14.01" — these are scheme A (single issuing authority) or B? Actually, OIML-CS has two schemes: Scheme A (issuing authority evaluates) and Scheme B (manufacturer's declaration with conformity verification). The certificate number format is typically "Rxxx/yyyy-AA-nn.nn". Without an explicit scheme letter, it's hard. Many R49 water meter certificates are Scheme A. Hmm.

The schema asks for scheme (A|B). Without explicit mention in markdown, I could omit it or infer. The rule says don't fabricate. But scheme is a required-ish field in the schema but listed as optional? The schema shows "number, scheme (A|B), project_number, page_total, member_state, date_issued, oiml_issuer_id". I'll omit scheme since not stated. Actually, wait — typical LNE OIML-CS certificates use "R49/2013-FR2-16.02" format. The "FR2" ... hmm. Actually OIML-CS format: "OIML Rxx/yyyy-X-nn.nn" where X is the country code. FR2? Sometimes "FR1" vs "FR2" to distinguish issuing authorities in the same country? LNE is the French issuing authority. The "2" might be a suffix. Anyway.
